source: NCERT Class XII, India — People and Economy, Ch. 9 (Planning and Sustainable Development in Indian Context).

sections.heading: 1. Planning in India
points: **Planning** = making conscious, coordinated decisions to achieve development goals.
Two approaches: **sectoral planning** (development of sectors like agriculture, industry) and **regional planning** (development of specific areas/regions).
The **Planning Commission (1950)** made **Five Year Plans**; replaced by the **NITI Aayog (2015)** — a think-tank for cooperative federalism.

sections.heading: 2. Target Area and Backward Area Planning
points: **Target-area/target-group planning** — focuses on **backward regions and weaker sections** to reduce disparity.
Programmes: **Hill Area Development, Drought-Prone Area Programme (DPAP), Tribal Area Development, Command Area Development**.
Aim: balanced regional development.

sections.heading: 3. Case Study — Bharmaur (Himachal)
points: **Bharmaur (Himachal Pradesh)** — a tribal region (the Gaddi shepherds), studied as an example of **integrated tribal development**.
Development brought roads, schools, health care and rising literacy (especially female literacy), transforming the region.
It shows how planning can uplift a backward area.

sections.heading: 4. Sustainable Development — Indira Gandhi Canal
points: **Sustainable development** = development that meets present needs without harming future generations.
**Case study — the Indira Gandhi Canal (Nahar), Rajasthan** — brought irrigation to the desert, transforming agriculture, but also caused **waterlogging, salinity and ecological problems**.
Lesson: development must be **ecologically sustainable** (balance growth with environment); measures like proper drainage, crop choice, eco-development.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Planning: sectoral vs regional; Planning Commission (1950) → NITI Aayog (2015).
Target-area planning: Hill Area, Drought-Prone Area (DPAP), Tribal Area programmes.
Bharmaur (Himachal) = integrated tribal development (Gaddi tribe).
Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan) = irrigation in the desert (but waterlogging/salinity).
Sustainable development = growth without harming future generations.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **Planning Commission (1950)** was replaced by the **NITI Aayog (2015)**.
**Bharmaur (Himachal Pradesh)** = case of **tribal area development** (Gaddi tribe).
The **Indira Gandhi Canal** is in **Rajasthan** (irrigation + waterlogging/salinity problems).
**Target-area planning** focuses on **backward regions/weaker sections**.
